rationale: A parallel cluster comparison gives the cleanest contrast: six boards switched on in February and five in December, with completeness compared between the groups from March to November (claims c1, c2 give the planning values; claim c3 supports time to treatment as a secondary outcome).
alternatives: Stepped-wedge design following the six-wave schedule
whyNotMoreComplex: A stepped-wedge design adds secular trend assumptions.

decision.statement: Allocate the 11 boards by chance to switch the template package on in February 2027 (six boards) or December 2027 (five boards), and compare documentation completeness between the two groups from March to November 2027.
decision.question: Does the template package increase complete decision documentation in tumour boards?

criteria.text: Templates and coordinators plausibly raise completeness by 20 points or more.
The digital team cannot switch on six boards in the same month.

gates.requirement: Research ethics approval covering the evaluation, with every board receiving the template in 2027
gates.evidence: Approval REB-CN-2026-118 dated 2026-08-29, supplied by the investigator

gates.requirement: Software licences and training capacity for six boards in February 2027

alternatives: Stepped-wedge design following the six-wave schedule
decision.note: Rests on ledger claims c1 to c3; the licensing gate is unknown.

summary: Parallel cluster comparison proposed; the licensing gate is unknown.
